# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). ## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-926: [CRAP] postPRReviewComments.js::action — CRAP 2010 (CC 168), highest-churn file: flatten into a tested pipeline

## Description

## Problem
`js/postPRReviewComments.js::action` has **CRAP 2010.5** (CC 168, 59.7% covered) — 530 lines (831–1368) of the PR-review post-processing leg, in the file with the highest churn in the repo (44 of the last 60 commits touch it, so every refactor conflicts and every bug fix is risky). The file has 15 over-threshold functions, ~2560 total CRAP.

## Goal
CRAP of `action` < 100 (stretch < 30) by turning it into a flat pipeline of named steps.

## Suggested approach
1. Pin current behaviour with characterization tests per verdict branch (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / re-review, formal review on/off, suggestions-only, dispatch-race guard, markers).
2. Extract: verdict + marker parsing, thread resolve/reply planning, label/status transitions, summary-comment building → pure functions returning a plan; keep one thin executor that performs the side effects in the **same order** as today.
3. Then attack the other 14 functions in the file, biggest first.

## Acceptance
- `action` CRAP < 100, file total CRAP down, no regression, review-leg tests green, identical comments/labels/transitions on the recorded fixtures.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

1. **IMPORTANT (behavioral divergence)**: `postInlineComment` fallback path lost the submodule 📍 prefix — when `addInlineComment` throws (e.g. 422), the original posted the fallback with the mutated `commentText` (including '📍 **path:line** (submodule content line)' prefix applied during submodule remap). New code catches at `postInlineComment` level and passes the original `commentText` — the prefix (in `plan.commentText`) is dropped. This violates the ticket's "identical comments" acceptance. Line 716 in new file — is it in the diff? Yes: `return fallbackInlineComment(scm, pullRequestId, filePath, inlineComment.line, commentText, error);` is an added line.

Wait — actually, let me double check the original: original code, in the catch, `postFallbackInlineComment(scm, pullRequestId, filePath, inlineComment.line, commentText)` — commentText by reference, mutated earlier if remap happened. Yes. Confirmed divergence.

2. Also in `applyFormalGithubReview`: original computed generalContent/approveBody OUTSIDE the try — exceptions there propagated up to action()'s catch (resulting in whole-leg failure). New code catches them inside (warn). This is a behavior change in error handling — but arguably improvement and resolveCommentFileReference is null-safe. Not worth flagging beyond SUGGESTION... Actually original: was generalContent outside try? From the diff:

```
-    var generalContent = resolveCommentFileReference(generalComment, ticketKey, workingDir) || generalComment;
-    var approveBody = (generalContent && String(generalContent).trim())
-        ? generalContent
-        : 'AI review approves this pull request.';
     try {
```

Yes, removed lines before `try {`. So in the original, if resolveCommentFileReference threw, applyFormalGithubReview threw → caught by action's outer catch → whole action returns failure. New: caught by inner catch → warn, continue. Divergence in failure mode. resolveCommentFileReference — let me check if it can throw. It reads a file if path-like. file_read could throw. So this is a real behavioral change in an error path: a formal-review content-resolution error previously aborted the entire leg (with error comment on ticket), now it's swallowed and the leg succeeds. Hmm — but is that a problem? The ticket says behavior-preserving. This one changes failure semantics. However the change arguably makes the system MORE robust. Severity: SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? It's in an opt-in path (formalGithubReview). I'd say SUGGESTION... but actually consider: previously the failure produced '❌ PR Review Error' on ticket; now silently continues. Silent behavior change. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (low risk, opt-in path).

3. Dead code check: `orZero`, `orNull`, `orEmpty` — used? orNull used in parseJobParamPRAnchor, prHeadRef. orZero in maxThreadLimitOf. orEmpty in folderKeyOf, parseLinkedIssueNumber, buildReviewContext. OK all used.

repoInfo resolution (with log 'Using targetRepository from config')
if (prAnchor) prNumber = prAnchor;
if (!repoInfo) warn
read pr_info.md (log 'Found PR info input folder: #')
search fallback
```

11. Log parity: 'PR number not found input folder, searching GitHub...' — new in searchMissingPRNumber via console.log. ✓. 'Could not find PR for ticket' warn in findPRViaSearch. ✓ 'Found PR via GitHub search: #'. ✓

12. `resolveRepoInfo` returns scm.getRemoteRepoInfo() without log — original same.

13. Potential issue: `buildReviewContext` computes `labels: ticketLabels(params.ticket)` — original computed labels AFTER scm creation and used in step 13b only. Same value. ✓

19. Subtle: original `if (prAnchor) prNumber = prAnchor;` — prNumber could be overridden by pr_info.md parse! 20. Now check the deletion-scan change more carefully — `trackDiffFileState` in `isFileDeletedInDiff` new version also processes `--- a/` lines: oldFile = oldFilePathOf (null if /dev/null). And on 'diff --git' sets currentFile AND oldFile to header path. For a deletion, header: `diff --git a/foo b/foo\n` then `deleted file mode 100644` — currentFile='foo' matches. ✓. But also for a normal modified file segment: `diff --git a/bar b/bar` ... `--- a/bar`, `+++ b/bar`, and if the diff for bar contains no 'deleted file mode', fine. What about a file where `deleted file mode` appears in the CONTENT? Impossible—content lines are prefixed with +/-/space in the diff. A context line ' deleted file mode...' starts with space, indexOf('deleted file mode')===0 fails. ✓ Safe.

BUT one regression risk: in the OLD isFileDeletedInDiff, currentFile was set from `+++ b/` line (post-header), so for a file that is both renamed-to and deleted... unrealistic. Also: quoted/renamed paths edge — headerPathOf parses `diff --git a/X b/Y` returning X (the a/ side). For a pure rename a/X → b/Y, currentFile='X' during that segment; a 'deleted file mode' doesn't appear. Fine.

What about `diff --git a/foo b/foo` for file foo where foo is deleted, and the target filePath is 'foo'? Works — fixes the actual bug. ✓

blocks.text:
The same failures (developTicketAndCreatePR, agentDocsCoverage) reproduce on origin/main — confirming they're pre-existing node-harness environment failures, not caused by this PR. The CI runs these via the GraalJS dmtools runner, which this environment can't replicate.

Conclusion on CI/tests: the PR's own module suite passes 91/91; full-suite failures are pre-existing env issues on main.

Now let me finish the deep review. Key findings so far:

1. **IMPORTANT (behavioral divergence)**: `postInlineComment` fallback path lost the submodule 📍 prefix — when `addInlineComment` throws (e.g. 422), the original posted the fallback with the mutated `commentText` (including '📍 **path:line** (submodule content line)' prefix applied during submodule remap). New code catches at `postInlineComment` level and passes the original `commentText` — the prefix (in `plan.commentText`) is dropped. This violates the ticket's "identical comments" acceptance. Line 716 in new file — is it in the diff? Yes: `return fallbackInlineComment(scm, pullRequestId, filePath, inlineComment.line, commentText, error);` is an added line.

Wait — actually, let me double check the original: original code, in the catch, `postFallbackInlineComment(scm, pullRequestId, filePath, inlineComment.line, commentText)` — commentText by reference, mutated earlier if remap happened. Yes. Confirmed divergence.

2. Also in `applyFormalGithubReview`: original computed generalContent/approveBody OUTSIDE the try — exceptions there propagated up to action()'s catch (resulting in whole-leg failure). New code catches them inside (warn). This is a behavior change in error handling — but arguably improvement and resolveCommentFileReference is null-safe. Not worth flagging beyond SUGGESTION... Actually original: was generalContent outside try? From the diff:

```
-    var generalContent = resolveCommentFileReference(generalComment, ticketKey, workingDir) || generalComment;
-    var approveBody = (generalContent && String(generalContent).trim())
-        ? generalContent
-        : 'AI review approves this pull request.';
     try {
```

Yes, removed lines before `try {`. So in the original, if resolveCommentFileReference threw, applyFormalGithubReview threw → caught by action's outer catch → whole action returns failure. New: caught by inner catch → warn, continue. Divergence in failure mode. resolveCommentFileReference — let me check if it can throw. It reads a file if path-like. file_read could throw. So this is a real behavioral change in an error path: a formal-review content-resolution error previously aborted the entire leg (with error comment on ticket), now it's swallowed and the leg succeeds. Hmm — but is that a problem? The ticket says behavior-preserving. This one changes failure semantics. However the change arguably makes the system MORE robust. Severity: SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? It's in an opt-in path (formalGithubReview). I'd say SUGGESTION... but actually consider: previously the failure produced '❌ PR Review Error' on ticket; now silently continues. Silent behavior change. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (low risk, opt-in path).

3. Dead code check: `orZero`, `orNull`, `orEmpty` — used? orNull used in parseJobParamPRAnchor, prHeadRef. orZero in maxThreadLimitOf. orEmpty in folderKeyOf, parseLinkedIssueNumber, buildReviewContext. OK all used.

4. Exports: the module.exports list grew by ~28 new exports — needed by tests. Fine.

5. `resolveBitriseBranch` is called twice in triggerBitriseBuild (branch + log) — pre-existing duplication retained; minor.

6. `buildBitriseEnvVars`: `(bitriseBuild.envVars || []).slice()` — same as original.

7. Check `postInlineCommentsIfPresent` — logs same.

8. `parsePRInfoMarkdown`: original only overwrote prUrl if urlMatch — new matchPRUrl(prInfo, current.prUrl) — fallback current. Same.

9. One more check — `resolveCustomParams` and statuses resolution order: original computed statuses AFTER the 'Review recommendation:' log. New: same order in action. Good.

10. `discoverPullRequest` — order: repoInfo resolved BEFORE reading pr_info (original: repoInfo first, then prAnchor prNumber, then warn if !repoInfo, then read pr_info.md). New: resolveRepoInfo, then warn if !repoInfo, then read pr_info + search. Wait original order:
```
repoInfo resolution (with log 'Using targetRepository from config')
if (prAnchor) prNumber = prAnchor;
if (!repoInfo) warn
read pr_info.md (log 'Found PR info input folder: #')
search fallback
```
New: resolveRepoInfo (same log), warn if !repoInfo, applyPRInfoMarkdown (pr starts with number: prAnchor), search. Same order. ✓

11. Log parity: 'PR number not found input folder, searching GitHub...' — new in searchMissingPRNumber via console.log. ✓. 'Could not find PR for ticket' warn in findPRViaSearch. ✓ 'Found PR via GitHub search: #'. ✓

12. `resolveRepoInfo` returns scm.getRemoteRepoInfo() without log — original same.

13. Potential issue: `buildReviewContext` computes `labels: ticketLabels(params.ticket)` — original computed labels AFTER scm creation and used in step 13b only. Same value. ✓

14. `machineAuthor: machineAuthorModule.resolveMachineAuthor(jp, config)` — original resolved after config load. ✓

15. `scm: scmModule.createScm(config)` in buildReviewContext — original same position. ✓

16. In the PR-anchored path, `finishPRAnchoredReview` — original wrapped addLabel in try with warn 'Failed to add ai_pr_reviewed to PR #X:'. New addPRLabelQuietlyDetailed(scm, pr.number, LABELS.AI_PR_REVIEWED, 'Failed to add ai_pr_reviewed to PR #...:') — logs warn(warnPrefix, err.message||err). Same. removeLabel 'agent:review' warn 'No agent:review label to remove from PR #'. ✓ (original same text). ✓

17. The re-arm linked issue: original logged 'Re-armed agent:rework on linked issue #N' where N = lm[1] (string). New: 'Re-armed agent:rework on linked issue #' + linkedIssue (number) — same printed value. addLabel(parseInt) vs addLabel(linkedIssue) — same number. ✓

18. `postReviewToJira(tracker, ctx.ticketKey, ctx.jiraReview, reviewData, pr.url)` — original prUrl. ✓

19. Subtle: original `if (prAnchor) prNumber = prAnchor;` — prNumber could be overridden by pr_info.md parse! In PR-anchored mode, if input/pr_info.md exists and has a different PR #, original would override prAnchor with the parsed number. New: same (pr starts with prAnchor, applyPRInfoMarkdown overwrites prNumber on match). ✓

20. Now check the deletion-scan change more carefully — `trackDiffFileState` in `isFileDeletedInDiff` new version also processes `--- a/` lines: oldFile = oldFilePathOf (null if /dev/null). And on 'diff --git' sets currentFile AND oldFile to header path. For a deletion, header: `diff --git a/foo b/foo\n` then `deleted file mode 100644` — currentFile='foo' matches. ✓. But also for a normal modified file segment: `diff --git a/bar b/bar` ... `--- a/bar`, `+++ b/bar`, and if the diff for bar contains no 'deleted file mode', fine. What about a file where `deleted file mode` appears in the CONTENT? Impossible—content lines are prefixed with +/-/space in the diff. A context line ' deleted file mode...' starts with space, indexOf('deleted file mode')===0 fails. ✓ Safe.

BUT one regression risk: in the OLD isFileDeletedInDiff, currentFile was set from `+++ b/` line (post-header), so for a file that is both renamed-to and deleted... unrealistic. Also: quoted/renamed paths edge — headerPathOf parses `diff --git a/X b/Y` returning X (the a/ side). For a pure rename a/X → b/Y, currentFile='X' during that segment; a 'deleted file mode' doesn't appear. Fine.

What about `diff --git a/foo b/foo` for file foo where foo is deleted, and the target filePath is 'foo'? Works — fixes the actual bug. ✓

21. In parseDiffLineInfo's new scanDiffLine: header lines processed for ANY file (parseTrackHeaderLine runs before the currentFile check) — same as original (diff --git/--- /+++ processed regardless of currentFile). ✓ Hunk header processed only when currentFile === filePath. ✓

22. Test file: uses arrow functions `(mocks && mocks.file_read) || function()...` — actually arrow at line ~55 `file_read: (mocks && mocks.file_read) || function() { return null; }`. Mixed styles but fine. …
